1 CORAM : MRS.VRUSHALI V. JOSHI, J.
RESERVED ON : OCTOBER 30th, 2023 PRONOUNCED ON : DECEMBER 11th, 2023 JUDGMENT 1.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 06.11.2004 passed by the Civil Judge Senior Division, Nagpur in Land Acquisition Case No.44/1998, the appellants have preferred this appeal.
The claimant/respondent has also filed cross-objection being not satisfied with the amount of compensation granted for orange trees.

2. The appellants/respondents have acquired total 3.81 hectares perennial irrigated land along with orange fruits bearing and other trees, Bunds, Well, Farm House, Pipe Lines etc. at Survey No.352 situated at mouza Ridhora, Tahasil and District Nagpur for construction of Dam under Lower Wanna Project in Land Acquisition Case No.2/A-65/1992-93.
3.

The cross-objector has filed the Reference Application under Section 18 of the land Acquisition Act against the award dated 30.04.1997 declared by the respondent No.1 i.e. appellant in Land Acquisition Case No.2/A-65/1992-93 of mouza Ridhora, Tahsil and District Nagpur.

The reference Court by its judgment enhanced the compensation for agricultural field at the rate of Rs.2,50,000/-
per hectare.
The cost of 730 Orange trees was determined at the rate of Rs.2,500/- per tree and the cost of 150 Bor fruit trees at the rate of Rs. 500/- per tree.
The appellants 3/5 FA.419.06-J.odt have preferred an appeal against the judgment which is admitted.
The cross objector though aggrieved by the determination of value of Rs.2,500/- per Orange tree, has not filed the cross-objection in time due to her personal difficulties.

The delay of filing cross-objection of 4761 days is condoned by this Court on 06.12.2022 and statutory benefits and interest on the delayed period was waived by the cross-objector/claimant.
4.
Heard learned Counsel for the appellant and the learned Assistant Government Pleader.
5. According to the learned Counsel for the appellants, the compensation enhanced by the reference Court for Orange trees was not justified and was without sufficient evidence.
The number of Orange trees is not 730, it is 702.
46 trees were held to be Forest trees.
Hence, the amount of compensation as granted was liable to be reduced.
6. The learned Counsel for the claimant submitted that the reference Court ought to have granted compensation at the rate of Rs.5000/- per Orange tree.
The 7/12 extract indicates presence of 730 Orange trees and 150 Bor trees as fruit bearing trees along with some other trees.

According to him,
in First Appeal No.699/2015 and Cross- Objection No.52/2016 (Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation Vs. Shivnarayan Gourishankar Tamhanpure (Jaiswal) (Dead) through his 4/5 FA.419.06-J.odt legal heirs) decided on 14.12.2020 by this Court has held, the claimants entitled for the compensation of Rs.5000/- per Orange tree on the basis of number of trees recorded in 7/12 extracts.

sentences.text:
The following point arises for determination :
"Whether the judgment of the reference Court deserves to be modified ?"
8. On perusal of the records of the case, it is seen that the claimants led evidence.
The witness to whom the claimant has examined is the qualified person of M.Sc. Horticultural and worked in Punjabrao Krishi Vidyapith, Nagpur as Associate Professor of Horticultural.
He is working as a Valuer of trees.
He visited the applicant's land in question and examined the trees in the said field.
He gave the report, which is at Exhibit 17, which shows that there are 730 Orange trees and 150 Bor trees.
The value of 730 Orange trees was valued at Rs.5,387 per tree and 150 Bor trees was valued at Rs.1,493/- per tree.
The reference Court has adopted the value of Orange trees in Land Acquisition Case No.43/1999 and granted Rs.2,500/- per tree for 730 Orange trees.
As regards the rate of compensation for Orange trees is concerned, it is seen that the valuer has found an amount of Rs.5437/- per tree as just compensation in his report.
The reference Court however has granted Rs.2,500/- per tree.
In First Appeal No.699/2015, Rs.5000/- per tree amount of compensation for the Orange trees is reasonable considering the nature of crop in that part of the area.
To that extent the judgment of the reference Court deserves modification.
The point as framed is answered accordingly.
10. The judgment of the reference Court is partly modified.
It is held that the claimant is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5000/- per tree for 730 Orange trees.
Rest of the award stands confirmed.
Cross- Objection No.92/2022
is partly allowed to that extent.
11. The claimant is at liberty to withdraw the balance of compensation deposited in the Court with accrued interest excluding the interest on delayed period.
The balance amount of compensation be deposited in the reference Court within a period of four months from today.
12. The First Appeal No.419/2006
stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.
